examples.ko: 바다 위에서 갈매기가 시끄럽게 울고 있어요.
examples.en: A seagull is crying loudly over the sea.

examples.ko: 배를 타면 갈매기에게 과자를 던져 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: On a boat, you can throw snacks to the seagulls.
The seagull cheering song at the Busan baseball stadium is famous.
White seagulls are flying around the beach.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 갈매기를 처음 봤을 때 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: When I first saw a seagull as a kid, I was startled.
Seagulls live by catching and eating fish.

explain: 바닷가 이야기에 자주 나오는 새예요. '갈매기가 날다', '갈매기가 울다'처럼 말해요. '갈매기살'은 이름만 같고 새가 아니라 돼지고기의 한 부위니까 메뉴판에서 놀라지 마세요.
explain_en: This is a bird that often appears in stories about the seaside. Koreans say '갈매기가 날다' or '갈매기가 울다'. '갈매기살' only shares the name; it is not the bird but a cut of pork, so don't be surprised when you see it on a menu.

examples.en: My grandfather spread manure on the field.
I'm collecting fallen leaves to use as fertilizer.
The vegetables grow well because the soil is well fertilized.

examples.ko: 음식물 쓰레기를 거름으로 만드는 방법이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a way to turn food waste into compost.
I closed the window because of the smell of manure.

examples.ko: 거름을 너무 많이 주면 식물이 죽을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you give too much fertilizer, the plant can die.

explain: 거름은 똥이나 낙엽처럼 자연에서 얻은 재료를 말하는 때가 많고, 공장에서 만든 것은 '비료'라고 해요. 도시에서는 '비료'가 더 흔해요. '걸음'(걷는 것)과 소리가 같아서 글자로 구별해야 해요.
explain_en: 거름 often refers to natural material such as dung or leaves, while factory-made products are called '비료'. In cities '비료' is more common. It sounds the same as '걸음' (a step), so tell them apart by spelling.

examples.en: On autumn nights you can hear crickets.
A cricket came into the room.
The kids searched the grass to catch a cricket.
Crickets make sound by rubbing their wings.
When I hear a cricket's chirp, I feel autumn.
I first saw a cricket at my grandmother's country house.

explain: 귀뚜라미 소리는 한국에서 가을을 알리는 소리로 자주 써요. 소리는 '귀뚤귀뚤'이라고 표현해요. 여름 매미와 짝으로 '매미는 여름, 귀뚜라미는 가을'이라고 느끼는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: In Korea, cricket sounds often signal autumn. The sound is written as 귀뚤귀뚤. Many people pair it with the summer cicada: 매미 for summer, 귀뚜라미 for fall.

en: floral scent; fragrance of a flower

examples.en: When I opened the window, the first thing I noticed was the scent of flowers.
Smelling flower fragrance makes me feel good.
The scent of flowers also comes carried on the spring breeze.
This scented candle has a gentle floral scent, which I like.
I was lost in the flower fragrance and stood there for a long time.

examples.ko: 꽃향기 때문에 재채기가 나는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people sneeze because of the scent of flowers.

explain: '냄새'보다 기분 좋은 느낌의 '향기'를 쓴 말이에요. '꽃향기를 맡다'처럼 '맡다'와 같이 써요. 가볍게는 '꽃냄새'라고도 하지만 좋은 향을 말할 때는 '꽃향기'가 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It uses '향기' (fragrance) rather than '냄새' (smell), so it has a pleasant feel. It pairs with '맡다', as in '꽃향기를 맡다'. People casually say '꽃냄새' too, but '꽃향기' suits a nice scent better.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나 보니 나팔꽃이 활짝 피었어요.
examples.en: When I woke up in the morning, the morning glories were in full bloom.
The child planted morning glory seeds in a pot.

examples.ko: 나팔꽃은 해가 뜨면 피고 오후에는 시들어요.
examples.en: Morning glories open when the sun rises and wilt in the afternoon.
Morning glory vines climb along the fence.
The morning glory is purple and so pretty.
I observed morning glories for my summer vacation homework.

explain: 꽃 모양이 나팔 같아서 붙은 이름이에요. 초등학교 여름방학 관찰 숙제에 자주 나오는 꽃이에요.
explain_en: The name comes from the flower's trumpet-like shape. It is a flower that often appears in elementary school summer observation homework.

examples.en: Snow blossoms covered the winter mountain.

examples.ko: 주말에 눈꽃을 보러 태백산에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: This weekend I am going to Taebaeksan to see the snow-covered trees.
Snow blossoms sparkle in the sunlight.
A snow blossom festival is being held, so there are many people.
She wore a dress as white as snow blossoms.

examples.ko: 눈꽃과 함께 찍은 사진이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The photo taken with the snow blossoms is really pretty.

explain: '눈꽃이 피다'처럼 눈이 나뭇가지에 하얗게 쌓인 모습을 꽃에 빗대어 말해요. 하늘에서 내리는 눈 한 알 한 알은 '눈송이'라고 해요.
explain_en: '눈꽃이 피다' compares snow piled white on branches to flowers in bloom. Each flake falling from the sky is a '눈송이'.

examples.en: On the southern coast, camellias bloom in winter.

examples.ko: 눈 위에 빨간 동백 꽃송이가 툭 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: A red camellia blossom dropped onto the snow.
I hear there was a time when people styled their hair with camellia oil.

examples.ko: 동백은 겨울에도 잎이 푸르러서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: Camellias stand out because their leaves stay green even in winter.

examples.ko: 동백 숲길을 걸으며 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took lots of photos while walking along the camellia forest path.

examples.ko: 엄마는 동백 그림이 있는 접시를 좋아하세요.
examples.en: Mom likes plates with a camellia painting.

explain: 동백은 겨울에서 봄 사이, 특히 제주도와 남쪽 바닷가에서 피는 붉은 꽃이에요. 꽃이 질 때 송이째 툭 떨어지는 모습이 특징이라 노래와 시에 자주 나와요. 나무와 꽃을 모두 동백이라고 불러요.
explain_en: 동백 is a red flower that blooms between winter and spring, especially on 제주도 and the southern coast. It drops whole blossoms at once when it fades, which is why it often appears in songs and poems. Both the tree and the flower are called 동백.

examples.ko: 정원에 두더지가 땅을 파서 구멍이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A mole dug in the garden and left holes.
Moles live underground, so their eyes are small.
I played the whack-a-mole game at the arcade.

examples.ko: 아이는 책에서 본 두더지가 귀엽다고 했어요.
examples.en: The child said the mole in the book was cute.
Farmers are worried because there are many moles in the fields.
It's a day when I want to hide underground like a mole.

explain: '두더지'는 땅속에 굴을 파고 사는 작은 동물이에요. 한국에서는 오락실의 '두더지 잡기' 게임으로 아이들에게도 친숙해요. 밭을 파헤치기도 해서 농사짓는 사람들은 골치 아파해요.
explain_en: 두더지 is a small animal that digs tunnels and lives underground. Children in Korea know it well through the arcade game 두더지 잡기. It also digs up fields, which gives farmers a headache.

examples.ko: 비가 그치고 하늘에 별이 드문드문 보였어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, a few stars could be seen here and there in the sky.

examples.ko: 그 길에는 가로등이 드문드문 서 있어요.
examples.en: Streetlights stand sparsely along that road.

examples.ko: 저는 일기를 드문드문 써서 빠진 날이 많아요.
examples.en: I write my diary only now and then, so many days are missing.

examples.ko: 시골 마을이라 집이 드문드문 흩어져 있어요.
examples.en: It's a country village, so the houses are scattered far apart.
I hear from that friend only once in a while.

examples.ko: 밤늦은 지하철에는 승객이 드문드문 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: Late at night, passengers sit sparsely on the subway.

explain: 공간에서는 사이가 멀리 떨어져 있는 모양, 시간에서는 간격이 길게 이어지는 모양에 써요. 반대로 '빽빽이', '촘촘히'는 사이가 가까운 모양이에요. '가끔'은 시간에만 쓰고, '드문드문'은 장소와 시간 모두에 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: In space it means things are spread far apart, and in time it means events happen with long gaps. The opposites are '빽빽이' and '촘촘히' (densely). '가끔' works only for time, while '드문드문' works for both place and time.

examples.en: I met a wild dog on the mountain path and was startled.

examples.ko: 들개는 무리를 지어 다니는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Wild dogs often move around in packs.
An abandoned dog sometimes becomes a stray.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 들개 때문에 걱정이 많아요.
examples.en: The villagers are very worried about the wild dogs.

examples.ko: 들개를 보면 가까이 가지 말고 피하세요.
examples.en: If you see a wild dog, avoid it and don't go near.

examples.ko: 다큐멘터리에서 아프리카 들개가 사냥하는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw African wild dogs hunting in a documentary.

explain: '들개'는 주인 없이 들이나 산에서 사는 개예요. 버려져서 떠도는 개는 '유기견'이라고 해요. '들'은 야생의 뜻을 더해서 '들고양이', '들꽃'처럼 쓰여요.
explain_en: '들개' is a dog with no owner that lives in fields or mountains. A dog that was abandoned and wanders is called a '유기견'. The prefix '들' adds a wild feel, as in '들고양이' and '들꽃'.

examples.en: Lightning kept flashing in the night sky.
I polished my shoes until they gleamed.

examples.ko: 차 위에서 햇빛이 번쩍거려서 눈이 부셨어요.
examples.en: Sunlight flashed off the car and dazzled my eyes.

examples.ko: 번쩍거리는 불빛 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of the flashing lights.
His gold necklace glitters.
A police car's lights are flashing in the distance.

explain: '번쩍이다'와 거의 같게 쓰는데, 빛이 계속 되풀이해서 나는 느낌이 있어요. '반짝거리다'보다 빛이 더 크고 강해요. 번개, 불빛, 윤이 나는 물건에 잘 써요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '번쩍이다', with a sense of light flashing repeatedly. The light is bigger and stronger than with '반짝거리다'. It suits lightning, flashing lights and shiny objects.

examples.en: The rosebuds are slowly opening.
Buds have formed all over the branches of the cherry tree.

examples.ko: 봉오리가 터지면 곧 꽃이 활짝 필 거예요.
examples.en: Once the buds burst, the flowers will bloom wide soon.
It is still a bud, but it already smells nice.
A single small bud bloomed by the window.

examples.ko: 봄비를 맞은 봉오리가 눈에 띄게 커졌어요.
examples.en: The buds that got the spring rain have grown noticeably bigger.

explain: 보통 '꽃봉오리'라는 말로 많이 써요. '꽃망울'도 비슷한 말이에요. '봉오리가 맺히다', '봉오리가 터지다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: People usually say '꽃봉오리' (flower bud). '꽃망울' is a similar word. It goes with set verbs, such as '봉오리가 맺히다' (buds form) and '봉오리가 터지다' (buds burst).

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 강의 수위가 높아졌어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the river's water level rose.

examples.ko: 수위를 보면 홍수가 올지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell if a flood is coming by looking at the water level.
A dam's water level changes by season.
When the water level dropped, the underside of the bridge could be seen.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 한강 수위가 위험 수준이라고 했어요.
examples.en: The news said the Han River's water level was at a danger level.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 폭력의 수위가 높아서 아이들은 볼 수 없어요.
examples.en: That film has a high level of violence, so children cannot watch it.

explain: '수위'는 강이나 댐 물의 높이를 말하는데, 영화나 말의 정도가 어디까지인지 말할 때도 써요. '수위가 높다'는 말에는 정도가 강하다는 느낌이 있어요. 물의 깊이는 '깊이', 높이는 '수위'로 구별해요. 소리가 같은 '수위'(守衛)는 건물을 지키는 사람이에요.

phrases.en: adjust the level; tone it down
phrases.nuance_ko: 물 높이가 아니라 말이나 행동의 세기를 알맞게 맞춘다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means not the water height but adjusting how strong your words or actions are.
phrases.en_equiv: tone it down; dial it back

explain_en: 수위 is the height of water in a river or dam, and it is also used for how strong or extreme something is, like a film or remark. 수위가 높다 carries the feeling that the degree is strong. 깊이 is the depth of the water, while 수위 is its level. The same-sounding 수위 (守衛) is a building guard.

examples.en: Fish breathe through their gills.
If the fish's gills are red, it is fresh.
I removed the gills and prepared the fish.

examples.ko: 물 밖에 나온 물고기가 아가미를 뻐끔거려요.
examples.en: The fish out of water gulps with its gills.
The fish got hurt because the net caught on its gills.

examples.ko: 손질할 때 아가미 쪽에 칼을 넣어요.
examples.en: When preparing it, I put the knife in near the gills.

explain: 물고기가 물속에서 숨 쉬는 기관이에요. 사람이 숨 쉬는 '폐'와 짝지어 기억하면 쉬워요. 생선을 살 때 아가미 색을 보고 신선한지 확인하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the organ fish use to breathe underwater. It helps to pair it with '폐' (lungs), which humans use to breathe. When buying fish, people sometimes check the gill color to see if it is fresh.

examples.en: My grandmother gathers medicinal herbs in the mountains.
This herb is good when you drink it as tea.
They sell dried herbs at the market.
The smell of herbs filled the house.
I received a soap made from medicinal herbs as a gift.
Which herb is good for a cold?

explain: 약으로 쓰는 풀은 '약초', 한약의 재료가 되는 풀뿌리나 열매까지 넓게 부를 때는 '약재'라고 해요. '약초를 캐다', '약초를 달이다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: A plant used as medicine is 약초, while 약재 is the wider word for any ingredient of herbal medicine, including roots and fruits. It pairs with set verbs like '약초를 캐다' (gather) and '약초를 달이다' (boil down).

examples.en: The weather agency forecast rain for tomorrow.
The broadcast is forecasting a typhoon.
They forecast snow for the weekend.
The weather turned cloudy as forecast.
They will forecast that tomorrow will be clear.
The weather report did not forecast rain.

explain: 주로 기상청이나 방송이 주어예요. 일상 대화에서는 '내일 비 온대요'처럼 전해 들은 말로 날씨를 말해요.
explain_en: The subject is usually the weather agency or a broadcaster. In daily talk people say 'naeil bi ondaeyo' (I hear it will rain tomorrow) instead.

examples.en: When autumn came, the leaves turned yellow.
One leaf fell from the branch.

examples.ko: 우리 집 화분 이파리에 먼지가 쌓였어요.
examples.en: Dust has settled on the leaves of my potted plant.
Bugs ate up all the leaves.

examples.ko: 상추 이파리를 크게 펴서 쌈을 싸요.
examples.en: I spread out a big lettuce leaf and make a wrap.
If the leaves wilt, give it more water.

explain: '잎'과 같은 대상을 말하지만 말할 때 더 편하고 정겹게 들려요. 나무뿐 아니라 풀이나 채소의 잎에도 써요. '이파리가 무성하다', '이파리가 시들다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the same thing as '잎' but sounds more casual and familiar in speech. It is used for the leaves of trees, grasses and vegetables alike. Common phrases are '이파리가 무성하다' and '이파리가 시들다'.

examples.en: Carp swim in the pond.
I fed the carp at the park.
Carp are fish that live a long time.
My grandfather likes carp fishing.
I saw a big carp at the market.
They say braised carp is good for your health.

explain: 잉어는 민물고기이고, 색이 화려한 관상용 잉어는 '비단잉어'라고 해요. 모양이 비슷한 붕어와 달리 잉어는 입가에 수염이 있어요.
explain_en: 잉어 is a freshwater fish, and the colorful ornamental kind is called 비단잉어. Unlike the similar-looking 붕어, 잉어 has barbels at the corners of its mouth.

examples.en: I went fishing at the reservoir on the weekend.

examples.ko: 가뭄 때문에 저수지 물이 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The water in the reservoir dropped a lot because of the drought.

examples.ko: 마을 뒤에 있는 저수지는 경치가 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: The reservoir behind the village has a really beautiful view.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 저수지가 가득 찼어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the reservoir filled up.

examples.ko: 저수지 둘레를 한 바퀴 걸으면 한 시간쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: Walking once around the reservoir takes about an hour.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 큰 저수지의 물을 마셔요.
examples.en: This city drinks water from a large reservoir.

explain: '댐'은 물을 막는 시설이고, 저수지는 물을 모아 둔 곳 자체를 말해요. 한국에서는 시골 저수지에서 낚시나 산책을 많이 해요. 호수와 달리 사람이 만든 곳이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: A 댐 (dam) is the structure that blocks water, while a 저수지 is the place where the water is stored. In Korea people often fish or walk around country reservoirs. Unlike a 호수 (lake), it feels man-made.

examples.en: When spring comes, violets bloom along the road.
While taking a walk, I found a violet by the roadside.
My mother likes handkerchiefs with a violet pattern.
Violets are small but smell nice.
The children played making rings out of violets.
Shall we plant some violets in the pot too?

explain: 봄에 길가나 풀밭에서 볼 수 있는 작은 꽃이에요. 보라색을 많이 떠올리지만 '노랑제비꽃', '흰제비꽃'처럼 다른 색도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a small flower you can see along roads and in meadows in spring. People often picture purple, but there are other colors too, like '노랑제비꽃' (yellow) and '흰제비꽃' (white).

examples.ko: 해가 질 때 하늘이 주황빛으로 물들어요.
examples.en: When the sun sets, the sky is tinged orange.
I waited for my friend under an orange street lamp.
The tangerines ripened and their orange color became vivid.

examples.ko: 난로 속 불꽃이 주황빛을 띠고 있어요.
examples.en: The flame inside the stove has an orange tint.

examples.ko: 주황빛은 보기만 해도 따뜻한 느낌이 들어요.
examples.en: Just looking at orange gives a warm feeling.

examples.ko: 저녁 노을이 바다 위에 주황빛 길을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The evening glow made an orange path over the sea.

explain: '주황색'이 색 이름이라면 '주황빛'은 노을이나 불빛에서 느껴지는 오렌지색 기운에 어울려요. '주홍빛'보다는 덜 붉고 귤색에 가까워요.
explain_en: If '주황색' is the color name, '주황빛' suits the orange tint you feel in a sunset or a light. It is less red than '주홍빛' and closer to the color of a tangerine.

examples.en: Fish swim by moving their fins.
A shark's dorsal fin rose above the surface.
A goldfish's fins are thin and soft like cloth.
I got my hand pricked by a fin while fishing.

examples.ko: 고래는 큰 지느러미로 물을 힘껏 쳤어요.
examples.en: The whale struck the water hard with its big fin.

examples.ko: 이 물고기는 지느러미가 다 떨어져 나갔어요.
examples.en: This fish has lost all of its fins.

explain: '등지느러미', '꼬리지느러미'처럼 위치 이름을 앞에 붙여요. 수영할 때 발에 끼는 '오리발'은 사람이 쓰는 도구라서 지느러미라고 하지 않아요.
explain_en: Put the position first: 등지느러미 (dorsal fin), 꼬리지느러미 (tail fin). The swim fins you wear on your feet are called 오리발, not 지느러미, because they are a human tool.

examples.en: The phone vibrates on the desk.
The floor shook when the train passed.

examples.ko: 소리가 나면 유리창이 진동하는 게 느껴져요.
examples.en: When there's a sound, I can feel the window vibrating.
The speaker vibrated hard, so my hand tickled.

examples.ko: 큰 트럭이 지나갈 때마다 집이 진동할 정도예요.
examples.en: Every time a big truck passes, the house shakes.
When the string vibrates, it makes a sound.

explain: 휴대폰, 스피커, 기계, 땅처럼 물체가 규칙적으로 흔들릴 때 써요. '떨다'는 사람 몸이나 목소리에 쓰고, '진동하다'는 물체에 써요. 휴대폰 '진동 모드'로 익숙한 말이고, 냄새가 아주 강할 때도 '냄새가 진동하다'라고 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새가 아주 강하게 퍼질 때 써요. 좋은 냄새에도 쓰지만 나쁜 냄새에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a smell spreads very strongly. It can describe a nice smell, but it is used more often for bad ones.
phrases.en_equiv: reek; be thick with a smell

explain_en: Use it when an object such as a phone, speaker, machine, or the ground shakes regularly. 떨다 is for a person's body or voice, while 진동하다 is for objects. You know it from the phone's '진동 모드', and it is also used for very strong smells.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 청개구리가 큰 소리로 울어요.
examples.en: When it rains, tree frogs croak loudly.

examples.ko: 풀잎 위에 작은 청개구리가 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: A small tree frog is sitting on a blade of grass.

examples.ko: 청개구리는 몸 색깔을 바꿀 수 있어요.
examples.en: Tree frogs can change their body color.
My younger sibling caught a tree frog and surprised me.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 읽은 청개구리 동화가 생각나요.
examples.en: I remember the tree frog fairy tale I read as a kid.
I can hear tree frogs by the pond.

explain: 청개구리는 몸이 초록색이고 작은 개구리예요. 한국 전래동화에 말을 늘 반대로 하는 청개구리가 나와서, 부모 말을 안 듣는 아이를 '청개구리 같다'고 놀리기도 해요. 일반 개구리는 그냥 '개구리'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 우리 아들은 청개구리 같아서 하라고 하면 안 해요.
phrases.en: My son is a contrary one: he won't do what I tell him to.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시키는 것과 반대로만 하는 사람을 놀릴 때 써요. 전래동화에서 나온 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tease someone who always does the opposite of what is asked. It comes from a folktale.

explain_en: 청개구리 is a small green frog. In a Korean folktale a tree frog always does the opposite of what it is told, so a child who ignores their parents is teased as '청개구리 같다'. Ordinary frogs are just '개구리'.

examples.ko: 나뭇가지에 파랑새 한 마리가 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: A bluebird is sitting on the branch.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 파랑새 동화책을 읽은 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I read a bluebird storybook.
They say the bluebird symbolizes happiness.
I heard a bluebird singing outside the window.

examples.ko: 행복은 멀리 있는 파랑새가 아니라 가까이에 있어요.
examples.en: Happiness is not a faraway bluebird; it is close by.
I bought a bluebird-shaped key ring.

explain: '파랑새'는 실제 새 이름이기도 하지만 한국에서는 '행복'을 뜻하는 상징으로 더 자주 써요. 이야기에서 '행복은 가까이에 있다'는 주제와 함께 많이 나와요. 새를 세는 말은 '마리'예요.
explain_en: 파랑새 is a real bird, but in Korea it is more often used as a symbol of happiness. It often appears with the theme that happiness is close at hand. Birds are counted with 마리.

examples.en: Before sunrise, the dawn sky looks bluish.
After swimming for a long time, my lips turned bluish.
A bluish light comes into the room.
The photo came out bluish, so I took it again.
The lake in the moonlight looks so faintly blue.
The early morning mist was bluish and mysterious.

explain: 완전한 파란색이 아니라 연하게 푸른빛이 도는 색이에요. 새벽 하늘, 달빛, 추워서 변한 입술처럼 '살짝 푸르게 보이는' 때 써요. 비슷한 '파르스름하다'는 좀 더 맑고 연한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes a color that is faintly blue rather than fully blue. Use it for things that look slightly blue, like dawn skies, moonlight or cold lips. The similar '파르스름하다' feels a bit lighter and clearer.

examples.en: Sunflowers have bloomed fully in the field.
Sunflowers bloom with yellow flowers in summer.
My grandmother shelled sunflower seeds for me.

examples.ko: 여름 여행 때 해바라기 밭에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On my summer trip I took pictures in a sunflower field.
I hung a sunflower painting by the window.
I looked up at the tall sunflower.

explain: 해를 따라 움직이는 모습에서 생긴 이름이에요. 노란 꽃잎이 크고 둥글어서 여름 꽃의 대표로 꼽혀요. 꽃이 지고 나면 먹는 씨앗이 남는데, 이것을 '해바라기씨'라고 해요.
explain_en: The name comes from how the flower seems to follow the sun. Its big, round yellow petals make it a symbol of summer flowers. After it fades, the edible seeds are called '해바라기씨'.
